rows.quote: Running workflows to execute the entire sequence, with built-in support for suspension, resumption, and streaming results.
rows.stance_reason: Reuse typed workflow suspension but supply UH supervisor stop reasons and denial budgets.

rows.what_it_does: Mastra scorers evaluate agent outputs and workflow-step outputs with model-graded, rule-based, and statistical methods. Sampling, trace evaluation, stored scores, and verdict gates support continuous quality checks.
rows.quote: Scorers are automated tests that evaluate Agents outputs using model-graded, rule-based, and statistical methods.
rows.stance_reason: Use scorer and gate ideas, extending them to multiple independent reviewer families and wave packets.

rows.what_it_does: Mastra workflow steps have schemas, IDs, state, suspension/resumption, and Studio status/log views. Time travel can replay individual steps after a run completes.
rows.quote: After a run completes, replay individual steps to inspect or retry them.
rows.stance_reason: Adopt step-level replay but retain explicit immutable attempt records.

rows.what_it_does: AgentKit networks combine agents, shared state, and a router; each agent may use its own model and provider. Agent definitions include role-oriented name, description, system prompt, model, and tools.
rows.version_or_commit: docs current; no release pin shown
rows.quote: Networks are Systems of Agents. Use Networks to create powerful AI workflows by combining multiple Agents.
rows.stance_reason: Reuse composable team roles and model selection, adding explicit effort/time/memory budgets.

rows.what_it_does: AgentKit networks run a router-agent loop and expose maxIter to cap iterations; the router may return undefined to stop. Shared state records outputs for later routing.
rows.version_or_commit: docs current; no release pin shown
rows.quote: A Network can specify an optional maxIter setting to limit the number of iterations.
rows.stance_reason: Iteration caps help bound loops but do not encode UH's stop reason taxonomy or resume notes.

rows.what_it_does: AgentKit state stores chronological interaction history and typed data shared by agents, tools, and routers. The network loop uses state to make subsequent routing decisions.
rows.version_or_commit: docs current; no release pin shown
rows.quote: The history system maintains a chronological record of all Agent interactions in your Network.
rows.stance_reason: Use shared typed state for context, but add durable run/task/attempt lifecycle records.

rows.what_it_does: The fetched OpenTelemetry page states that GenAI semantic conventions moved to a dedicated repository and is no longer maintained in the old location. This confirms the convention surface is evolving and version-sensitive.
rows.quote: GenAI semantic conventions have moved to the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions repository.
rows.stance_reason: Track the moving standard but keep UH evidence schemas versioned and privacy-filtered independently.

rows.what_it_does: Langfuse records usage and USD cost per LLM generation, either ingested from provider responses or inferred from model definitions. Ingested values take priority, and model definitions can include pricing tiers.
rows.quote: Langfuse tracks the usage and cost of every LLM call in your application.
rows.stance_reason: Adopt measured-versus-inferred precedence but add stop-reason dimensions and unknown never zero.

rows.what_it_does: Langfuse distinguishes ingested usage/cost from inferred cost, supports custom model definitions and pricing tiers, and explicitly warns that missing reasoning-token usage prevents correct inference for some models.
rows.quote: When both are available, ingested values take priority over inferred ones.
rows.stance_reason: The explicit distinction between measured and inferred values matches UH cost truth requirements.

rows.what_it_does: Langfuse accepts OTLP traces at a documented endpoint, maps OTel attributes to its data model, and cautions against putting sensitive information in propagated baggage. It supports HTTP JSON and protobuf, not gRPC.
rows.quote: Do not include sensitive information (passwords, API keys, personal data, etc.) in baggage.
rows.stance_reason: Use OTLP ingestion and propagation guidance, but enforce UH prompt/secret exclusion at emission.

rows.what_it_does: AgentOps automatically instruments supported agent frameworks and records each execution as a session. Its dashboard presents execution duration, event breakdowns, LLM calls, and traces for debugging.
rows.version_or_commit: v2 docs current; repo main metadata checked 2026-09-15
rows.quote: After setting up AgentOps, each execution of your program is recorded as a session.
rows.stance_reason: Use session-level observability as evidence, but require explicit provider cost truth and stop reasons.

rows.what_it_does: AgentOps models executions as sessions and records traces, actions, tool calls, errors, and LLM calls for later drilldown. It is primarily an observability record, not a durable supervisor state machine.
rows.version_or_commit: v2 docs current; repo main metadata checked 2026-09-15
rows.quote: Most powerful of all is the Session Waterfall. On the left, a time visualization of all your LLM calls, Action events, Tool calls, and Errors.
rows.stance_reason: Use trace concepts for observability but do not substitute sessions for authoritative lifecycle state.

rows.what_it_does: Braintrust evaluations define data, a task, and scoring functions, then compare approaches and catch regressions. The platform supports traces, human feedback, datasets, and experiments in a workflow.
rows.version_or_commit: docs current; no release pin shown
rows.quote: Each evaluation consists of three components: Data, Task, Scores.
rows.stance_reason: Use evaluator structure and regression comparisons, extending to independent reviewer model families.

rows.what_it_does: Braintrust traces expose complete inputs and outputs, token counts, latency, cost, model configuration, and metadata in its logs. Its quickstart directs users to configure SDK tracing and verify traces appear.
rows.version_or_commit: docs current; no release pin shown
rows.quote: Click into any trace to see the complete input and output, token counts, latency, cost, model configuration, and metadata.
rows.stance_reason: Its trace fields are useful, but UH must exclude prompts and secrets from evidence schemas by design.

rows.what_it_does: Promptfoo evaluates prompts, models, and applications through declarative test cases, configurable metrics, matrix views, and structured results. It also supports automated red-team probes and risk reports.
rows.quote: promptfoo is an open-source CLI and library for evaluating and red-teaming LLM apps.
rows.stance_reason: Adopt declarative deliverable/evaluation checks but add UH-specific path, secret, and terminal-line scans.

rows.what_it_does: Promptfoo's GitHub Action compares before and after evaluations on pull requests and posts result links. Its red-team documentation describes systematic adversarial generation, automated scoring, and CI/CD integration.
rows.quote: On every pull request that modifies a prompt, the action will automatically run a full comparison.
rows.stance_reason: Reuse before/after quality evidence, adding multiple reviewer breadth and wave-level packets.

rows.what_it_does: SWE-bench evaluates generated patches against real GitHub issues in reproducible Docker environments. Its v5 CLI records run IDs and evaluation logs/results for later reporting.
rows.version_or_commit: main; v5 CLI visible in README
rows.quote: SWE-bench is a benchmark for evaluating large language models on real world software issues collected from GitHub.
rows.stance_reason: Use containerized reproducibility and run IDs as a model for deliverable validation evidence.

rows.what_it_does: SWE-bench provides gold/reference and prediction evaluation modes, result caching by run and instance IDs, and parallel workers. It measures patch resolution rather than reviewer diversity.
rows.version_or_commit: main; v5 CLI visible in README
rows.quote: The run summary is written to logs/evaluation/<run_id>/results.json.
rows.stance_reason: Adopt reproducible result packets while adding independent reviewer model-family breadth.

rows.what_it_does: AgentEvals evaluates agent trajectories, including intermediate tool-call steps, with strict/unordered/subset/superset matching and LLM-as-judge evaluators. Results include a score and reasoning/comment.
rows.quote: This package contains a collection of evaluators and utilities for evaluating the performance of your agents, with a focus on agent trajectory.
rows.stance_reason: Trajectory evaluation directly supports review breadth and tool-structure evidence.

rows.what_it_does: MCP defines tools/list and tools/call, schemas, annotations, and an explicit warning that tool annotations are untrusted unless from trusted servers. It recommends a human able to deny invocations.
rows.quote: For trust & safety and security, there SHOULD always be a human in the loop with the ability to deny tool invocations.
rows.stance_reason: Use MCP tool discovery and denial semantics, adding UH path-only matching and tamper detection.

rows.what_it_does: MCP roots let clients expose filesystem boundaries to servers and require clients to validate root URIs and permissions. The security guidance says servers should respect root boundaries and validate paths.
rows.quote: Roots define the boundaries of where servers can operate within the filesystem.
rows.stance_reason: Roots inform worker scope, but UH still needs per-worker credentials and sensitive-path deny-read.

rows.what_it_does: MCP sampling requires clients to control model access, selection, and permissions, with human review before request forwarding and response delivery. Clients should return a user-rejected error.
rows.quote: There SHOULD always be a human in the loop with the ability to deny sampling requests.
rows.stance_reason: MCP's explicit approval boundary supports rejecting auto-promotion under human gates.

rows.what_it_does: MCP roots require file:// URIs and can list multiple repositories, making filesystem boundaries transportable as URI values. The spec requires clients to validate root URIs against path traversal.
rows.quote: This MUST be a file:// URI in the current specification.
rows.stance_reason: Use URI roots for portable artifacts, adding platform-specific normalization and canonicalization.

rows.what_it_does: The 2025-06-18 MCP specification requires explicit user consent for data access, operations, tools, and sampling. It also defines response errors such as user rejection for sampling.
rows.quote: Users must explicitly consent to and understand all data access and operations.
rows.stance_reason: Adopt explicit consent and denial as first-class approval records.

rows.what_it_does: MCP security guidance requires user consent before exposing data and limits server visibility into prompts during sampling. It explicitly treats tool descriptions and annotations as potentially untrusted.
rows.quote: The protocol intentionally limits server visibility into prompts.
rows.stance_reason: Use MCP's consent and prompt-visibility constraints to shape evidence schemas that exclude sensitive content.

rows.what_it_does: The original gsd-build/gsd-2 repository is an archive redirect; current GSD Pi describes autonomous workflows that plan, implement, verify, and advance milestones and tasks. It stores summaries and validation evidence locally.
rows.quote: This repository is no longer the active home for GSD 2 development.
rows.stance_reason: The requested repository is archived, so behavior must be reverified against the moved project before adoption.

rows.what_it_does: GSD Pi documents artifacts such as plans, summaries, validation notes, and reports, plus structured JSON quick-task results and meaningful exit codes. It maintains local .gsd state and reviewable markdown projections.
rows.quote: Produces artifacts such as plans, summaries, validation notes, and reports.
rows.stance_reason: Use artifact and validation-note concepts while adding UH terminal-line and secret-like scans.

rows.what_it_does: GSD Pi stores planning and runtime state under .gsd, tracks work in a local database with markdown projections, and supports worktree-aware automation. The README identifies v1.20.0 as the latest release.
rows.quote: Tracks project state in a local database with markdown projections for review.
rows.stance_reason: Adopt durable local projections, keeping UH's attempt identity and cross-platform path contract.

rows.what_it_does: OMC's Team surface uses a staged team-plan, team-prd, team-exec, team-verify, and team-fix loop. It also documents persistent execution and a lead-session responsibility for final approval.
rows.quote: Team runs as a staged pipeline: team-plan → team-prd → team-exec → team-verify → team-fix (loop).
rows.stance_reason: Reuse staged execution and verification, adding explicit denial and stall budgets.

rows.what_it_does: OMC supports teams of Codex, Gemini, Antigravity, Grok, Cursor, and Claude workers and assigns role-oriented tasks such as critic, code-reviewer, security-reviewer, and test-engineer. Final approval remains a lead-session responsibility.
rows.quote: Cursor also supports reviewer-style roles (critic, code-reviewer, security-reviewer, test-engineer).
rows.stance_reason: Use distinct reviewer roles and model families as a breadth precedent, adding wave packet schemas.

rows.what_it_does: OMX provides a workflow layer around Codex with explicit commands for clarification, planning, durable goals, and team execution. It supports model/reasoning flags and worktree launch isolation.
rows.version_or_commit: main; README has no release version
rows.quote: It keeps Codex as the execution engine and makes it easier to start a stronger Codex session by default and run one consistent workflow from clarification to completion.
rows.stance_reason: Reuse durable objective/checkpoint workflow, adding a formal per-worker contract.

rows.what_it_does: OMX's canonical workflow includes plan, ultragoal, team, code-review, and ultraqa surfaces, with team used when a story needs coordinated parallel work. It recommends worktree isolation for concurrent sessions.
rows.version_or_commit: main; README has no release version
rows.quote: Use $team inside that execution path only when a specific Ultragoal story needs coordinated parallel work.
rows.stance_reason: Adopt selective team shapes and worktree isolation, adding independent reviewer-family requirements.

rows.what_it_does: OMX stores plans, logs, memory, and mode tracking under .omx and describes durable goals with checkpoints. Standard sessions use a single writable session pointer and fail closed on same-root conflicts.
rows.version_or_commit: main; README has no release version
rows.quote: It keeps project guidance, plans, logs, and state in .omx/.
rows.stance_reason: Use durable local state and fail-closed ownership, separating UH run/task/attempt identities.

rows.what_it_does: Across Paperclip, Orca, Temporal, LangGraph, Mastra, AgentKit, OTel, Langfuse, AgentOps, Braintrust, Promptfoo, SWE-bench, AgentEvals, MCP, GSD Pi, OMC, and OMX, the fetched mechanisms expose tools, approval, or roots but no documented combination of path-only matching, substitute-action deny reasons, and tamper detection.
rows.quote: Clients MUST consider tool annotations to be untrusted unless they come from trusted servers.
rows.stance_reason: Searched the full named scope for path-only guards and tamper detection; found no system documenting all three together.

rows.what_it_does: The named systems provide evaluation, tracing, or artifact reports, but the fetched sources do not document one deliverable scan combining dangling paths, fingerprint phrases, secret-like strings, stray files, and a required DONE/BLOCKED final line.
rows.quote: Score outputs automatically by defining metrics.
rows.stance_reason: Searched named evaluation and orchestration systems; found no source documenting the complete filesystem-and-terminal deliverable scan.

rows.what_it_does: The fetched orchestration systems expose iteration caps, state, queues, or concurrency settings, but none documents deriving a worker memory cap from declared parallelism as a first-class policy.
rows.version_or_commit: docs current; no release pin shown
rows.quote: A Network can specify an optional maxIter setting to limit the number of iterations.
rows.stance_reason: Searched all named orchestration systems for parallelism-derived memory accounting; found iteration/concurrency controls but no such derivation.
